sailing.d: To be impelled or driven forward by the action of wind upon sails, as a ship on water; to be impelled on a body of water by steam or other power.

sample.d: A part or snippet of something taken or presented for inspection, or shown as evidence of the quality of the whole; a specimen.

sausage.d: A food made of ground meat (or meat substitute) and seasoning, packed in a section of the animal's intestine, or in a similarly cylindrical shaped synthetic casing.

scarf.d: A long, often knitted, garment worn around the neck.

schedule.d: A slip of paper; a short note.

schoolwork.d: Work done for school, including both in class and as homework.
schoolwork.e: I'm 40, but now that I'm back going for my degree I'm swamped with schoolwork.

scientific.d: Related or connected to science: Derived from or consistent with the scientific method. In accord with the procedures, methods, conduct and accepted conventions of modern science.

scissors.d: One blade on a pair of scissors.
scissors.e: Scissors are used to cut the flowers.

scream.d: A loud, emphatic, exclamation of extreme emotion, especially horror, fear, excitement, or anger; it may comprise a word or a sustained, high-pitched vowel sound.
scream.e: He almost hit a pole, the way he came screaming down the hill.

screen.d: A physical barrier that shelters or hides. A physical divider intended to block an area from view, or provide shelter from something dangerous.

screw.d: A device that has a helical function. A simple machine, a helical inclined plane. A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a partially or completely threaded shank, sometimes with a threaded point, and a head used to both hold the top material and to drive the screw either directly into a soft material or into a prepared hole. A ship's propeller. An Archimedes screw. A steam vessel propelled by a screw instead of wheels.

seafood.d: Fish, shellfish, seaweed, and other edible aquatic life.

secret.d: A piece of knowledge that is hidden and intended to be kept hidden.
secret.e: "Can you keep a secret?" "Yes." "So can I."

secretary.d: Someone entrusted with a secret; a confidant.

seed.d: A fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant.
seed.e: If you plant a seed in the spring, you may have a pleasant surprise in the autumn.

seek.d: The operation of navigating through a stream.

semester.d: Half of a school year or academic year such as fall or spring semester.

send.d: To make something (such as an object or message) go from one place to another (or to someone).
send.e: Good thing I didn't hit send on that resume; I just noticed a bad typo.

senior.e: He was four years her senior.

sense.d: Any of the manners by which living beings perceive the physical world: for humans sight, smell, hearing, touch, taste.

separate.d: (usually in the plural) Anything that is sold by itself, especially an article of clothing.
separate.e: Separate the articles from the headings.

seriously.d: (manner) In a serious or literal manner.
seriously.e: He was hoping that we would take him seriously.

serve.d: An act of putting the ball or shuttlecock in play in various games.

several.d: An area of land in private ownership (as opposed to common land).

shade.d: Darkness where light, particularly sunlight, is blocked.
shade.e: The old oak tree gave shade in the heat of the day.

shall.d: Used before a verb to indicate the simple future tense in the first person singular or plural.
shall.e: I shall sing in the choir tomorrow.

shampoo.d: A traditional Indian and Persian body massage given after pouring warm water over the body and rubbing it with extracts from herbs.
shampoo.e: My neat-freak of a friend has been compulsively shampooing for every bath he has taken.

shape.d: The status or condition of something
shape.e: The used bookshop wouldn’t offer much due to the poor shape of the book.

shell.d: A hard external covering of an animal. The calcareous or chitinous external covering of mollusks, crustaceans, and some other invertebrates.
shell.e: In some mollusks, as the cuttlefish, the shell is concealed by the animal's outer mantle and is considered internal.

shine.d: Brightness from a source of light.

shock.e: The train hit the buffers with a great shock.

shore.d: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
shore.e: lake shore;  bay shore;  gulf shore;  island shore;  mainland shore;  river shore;  estuary shore;  pond shore;  sandy shore;  rocky shore

shout.d: A loud burst of voice or voices; a violent and sudden outcry, especially that of a multitude expressing joy, triumph, exultation, anger, or great effort.

sightseeing.d: To go sightseeing; to visit places of interest in a city, town or geographical area.
sightseeing.e: Sightseeing is a frequent reason to visit San Francisco.

silver.d: A lustrous, white, metallic element, atomic number 47, atomic weight 107.87, symbol Ag.
silver.e: to silver a pin;  to silver a glass mirror plate with an amalgam of tin and mercury

similar.d: That which is similar to, or resembles, something else, as in quality, form, etc.

simple.d: A herbal preparation made from one plant, as opposed to something made from more than one plant.

since.d: From a specified time in the past.

single.d: A 45 RPM vinyl record with one song on side A and one on side B.
single.e: Can you give me a single reason not to leave right now?

singular.d: (grammar) A form of a word that refers to only one person or thing.
singular.e: A singular experiment cannot be regarded as scientific proof of the existence of a phenomenon.

sink.d: A basin used for holding water for washing.

situation.d: The combination of circumstances at a given moment; a state of affairs.
situation.e: The United States is in an awkward situation with debt default looming.

sleepy.d: The gum that builds up in the eye; sleep, gound.

smooth.d: Something that is smooth, or that goes smoothly and easily.
smooth.e: We hope for a smooth transition to the new system.

society.d: A long-standing group of people sharing cultural aspects such as language, dress, norms of behavior and artistic forms.
society.e: This society has been known for centuries for its colorful clothing and tight-knit family structure.

soft.d: A soft or foolish person; an idiot.
soft.e: My head sank easily into the soft pillow.

software.d: Encoded computer instructions, usually modifiable (unless stored in some form of unalterable memory such as ROM).

soldier.d: A member of an army, of any rank.

solution.d: A homogeneous mixture, which may be liquid, gas or solid, formed by dissolving one or more substances.

somewhere.d: Unspecified or unknown (unlocated) place or location.
somewhere.e: I must have left my glasses somewhere.

source.d: The person, place or thing from which something (information, goods, etc.) comes or is acquired.
source.e: The accused refused to reveal the source of the illegal drugs she was selling.

spaghetti.d: A type of pasta made in the shape of long thin strings.
spaghetti.e: The cables spaghettied onto the shoulder of the technician.

spoon.d: An implement for eating or serving; a scooped utensil whose long handle is straight, in contrast to a ladle.
spoon.e: Sarah spooned some apple sauce onto her plate.

spread.d: To stretch out, open out (a material etc.) so that it more fully covers a given area of space.
spread.e: He spread his newspaper on the table.

stamp.d: An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
stamp.e: The horse gave two quick stamps and rose up on its hind legs.

state.d: A condition; a set of circumstances applying at any given time.

statue.d: A three-dimensional work of art, usually representing a person or animal, usually created by sculpting, carving, molding, or casting.

steal.d: To take illegally, or without the owner's permission, something owned by someone else without intending to return it.
steal.e: Three irreplaceable paintings were stolen from the gallery.

storm.d: Any disturbed state of the atmosphere, especially as affecting the earth's surface, and strongly implying destructive or unpleasant weather.
storm.e: The proposed reforms have led to a political storm.

stranger.d: Not normal; odd, unusual, surprising, out of the ordinary.
stranger.e: That gentleman is a stranger to me.  Children are taught not to talk to strangers.

strategy.d: The science and art of military command as applied to the overall planning and conduct of warfare.

strongly.d: In a strong or powerful manner.
strongly.e: The Pope feels strongly about the need for both sides of the armed conflict to return to the negotiating table.

structure.d: A cohesive whole built up of distinct parts.
structure.e: The birds had built an amazing structure out of sticks and various discarded items.

stuff.d: Miscellaneous items or objects; (with possessive) personal effects.
stuff.e: What is all that stuff on your bedroom floor?  He didn't want his pockets to bulge so he was walking around with all his stuff in his hands.

succeed.d: To follow something in sequence or time.

success.d: The achievement of one's aim or goal.
success.e: His third attempt to pass the entrance exam was a success.

successfully.d: In a successful manner; with success; without failing.

such.d: Like this, that, these, those; used to make a comparison with something implied by context.
such.e: I’ve never seen such clouds in the sky before.

sudden.d: Occurring quickly with little or no warning or expectation; instantly.
sudden.e: The sudden drop in temperature left everyone cold and confused.

suggest.d: To imply but stop short of saying explicitly.
suggest.e: Are you suggesting that I killed my wife?

suit.d: A set of clothes to be worn together, now especially a man's matching jacket and trousers (also business suit or lounge suit), or a similar outfit for a woman.
suit.e: Nick hired a navy-blue suit for the wedding.

suitable.d: Having sufficient or the required properties for a certain purpose or task; appropriate to a certain occasion.

suitcase.d: A large (usually rectangular) piece of luggage used for carrying clothes, and sometimes suits, when travelling.

summary.d: An abstract or a condensed presentation of the substance of a body of material.
summary.e: A summary review is in the appendix.

sunflower.d: Any plant of the genus Helianthus, so called probably from the form and color of its floral head, having the form of a large disk surrounded by yellow ray flowers. The commonly cultivated species, Helianthus annuus, a native of America.

sunglasses.d: Tinted glasses worn to protect the eyes from the sun.

sunlight.d: All the electromagnetic radiation given off by the Sun; especially, that in the visible spectrum and that bathes the Earth.
sunlight.e: Sunlight on the skin gives you vitamin D.

superlative.d: Having the power to carry something or someone above, over or beyond others.

superstar.d: Someone who has accumulated a vast amount of fame; a high-level celebrity.

supper.d: An optional light meal consumed shortly before going to bed.

support.e: Don't move that beam! It's a support for the whole platform.

surname.d: The portion of a person's name that is generally hereditary or treated as an indicator of a person's family, which may be shared with other members of the family, or otherwise derived from their names in some fashion; distinguished from that person's given name(s).
surname.e: James is my first name, and Smith is my surname.

survive.d: Of a person, to continue to live; to remain alive.

sweat.d: Fluid that exits the body through pores in the skin usually due to physical stress and/or high temperature for the purpose of regulating body temperature and removing certain compounds from the circulation.
sweat.e: Just thinking about the interview tomorrow puts me into a nervous sweat.

sweater.d: A knitted jacket or jersey, usually of thick wool, worn by athletes before or after exercise.

symbol.d: A character or glyph representing an idea, concept or object.
symbol.e: $ is the symbol for dollars in the US and some other countries.

system.d: A collection of organized things; a whole composed of relationships among its members.
system.e: There are eight planets in the solar system.

tape.d: Flexible material in a roll with a sticky surface on one or both sides; adhesive tape.
tape.e: Hand me some tape. I need to fix a tear in this paper.

tear.d: A hole or break caused by tearing.
tear.e: A small tear is easy to mend, if it is on the seam.

temperature.d: A measure of cold or heat, often measurable with a thermometer.
temperature.e: The temperature in the room dropped nearly 20 degrees; it went from hot to cold.

text.d: A writing consisting of multiple glyphs, characters, symbols or sentences.
text.e: I'll text the address to you as soon as I find it.

themselves.d: The reflexive case of they, the third-person plural personal pronoun. The group of people, animals or objects previously mentioned, as the object of a verb or following a preposition (also used for emphasis).
themselves.e: They are going to try climbing Mount Everest themselves.

therefore.d: For that or this purpose, referring to something previously stated.
therefore.e: Traditional values will always have a place, therefore they will never lose relevance.

thief.d: One who carries out a theft.

thirsty.e: After all that work I am really thirsty.

thought.d: To ponder, to go over in one's head.
thought.e: Idly, the detective thought what his next move should be.

thousand.e: Many thousands of people came to the conference.

tidy.e: She always kept her desk immaculately tidy; nothing was ever out of place.

tights.d: A close-fitting, sheer or non-sheer skin-tight garment worn principally by women and girls that covers the body completely from the waist down, usually including the feet.

till.d: Until; to, up to; as late as (a given time).
till.e: She stayed till the very end.

timetable.d: A tabular schedule of events with the times at which they occur, especially times of arrivals and departures.
timetable.e: The timetable has been changed several times since it was first announced.

title.d: A prefix (honorific) or suffix (post-nominal) added to a person's name to signify either veneration, official position or a professional or academic qualification. See also
title.e: a good title to an estate, or an imperfect title

toast.e: I ate a piece of toast for breakfast.

toe.d: Each of the five digits on the end of the foot.

toothache.d: A pain or ache in a tooth.

toothbrush.d: A brush, used with toothpaste, for cleaning the teeth. [from 17th c.]

tour guide.d: A person who provides assistance and information to people on organised tours.

tourist.d: Someone who travels for pleasure rather than for business.

toward.d: Yielding, pliant; docile; ready or apt to learn; not froward.

track.d: A mark left by something that has passed along.
track.e: Can you see any tracks in the snow?

trade.d: Buying and selling of goods and services on a market.
trade.e: I did no trades with them once the rumors started.

tradition.d: A part of culture that is passed from person to person or generation to generation, possibly differing in detail from family to family, such as the way to celebrate holidays.

traditional.e: I think her traditional values are antiquated.

traffic.d: Moving pedestrians or vehicles, or the flux or passage thereof.
traffic.e: The traffic is slow during rush hour.

traffic light.d: A signalling device positioned at a road intersection or pedestrian crossing to indicate when it may be safe to drive, ride or walk, using a universal colour code.

training.e: She trained seven hours a day to prepare for the Olympics.

tram.d: A passenger vehicle for public use that runs on tracks in the road (called a streetcar or trolley in North America).

trick.d: Something designed to fool, dupe, outsmart, mislead or swindle.
trick.e: It was just a trick to say that the house was underpriced.

trouble.e: He was in trouble when the rain started.

truly.d: (manner) In accordance with the facts; truthfully, accurately.
truly.e: That is truly all I know.

trust.d: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.
trust.e: He needs to regain her trust if he is ever going to win her back.

truth.d: True facts, genuine depiction or statements of reality.
truth.e: The truth is that our leaders knew a lot more than they were letting on.

understand.d: To grasp a concept fully and thoroughly, especially (of words, statements, art, etc.) to be aware of the meaning of and (of people) to be aware of the intent of.

unfortunately.d: Happening through bad luck, or because of some unfortunate event.
unfortunately.e: He unfortunately placed his hand on a loose brick.

unhealthy.d: Characterized by, or conducive to poor health.
unhealthy.e: The villagers lived in unhealthy surroundings.

unit.d: Oneness, singularity, seen as a component of a whole number; a magnitude of one.
unit.e: The centimetre is a unit of length.

university.d: Institution of higher education (typically accepting students from the age of about 17 or 18, depending on country, but in some exceptional cases able to take younger students) where subjects are studied and researched in depth and degrees are offered.
university.e: The only reason why I haven't gone to university is because I can't afford it.

unknown.d: Not known; unidentified; not well known.
unknown.e: The concept has existed since times unknown.

unlike.d: Not like; dissimilar (to); having no resemblance; unalike.
unlike.e: The brothers are quite unlike each other.

unnecessary.e: The automatic child-frightener made clowns unnecessary.

upset.e: He was upset when she refused his friendship.

upstairs.e: They can sleep in the upstairs bedroom.

used.e: soldiers who are used to hardships and danger

usual.d: The typical state of something, or something that is typical.

value.d: The quality that renders something desirable or valuable; worth.
value.e: There is tremendous value in a good education.

view.e: a fine view of Lake George

village.d: A rural habitation of size between a hamlet and a town.
village.e: There are 2 churches and 3 shops in our village.

violin.d: A musical four-string instrument, generally played with a bow or by plucking the string, with the pitch set by pressing the strings at the appropriate place with the fingers; also any instrument of the violin family.
violin.e: The first violin often plays the lead melody lines in a string quartet.

visitor.d: Someone who visits someone else; someone staying as a guest.

vocabulary.d: A usually alphabetized and explained collection of words e.g. of a particular field, or prepared for a specific purpose, often for learning.
vocabulary.e: My Russian vocabulary is very limited.

voice.d: Sound uttered by the mouth, especially by human beings in speech or song; sound thus uttered considered as possessing some special quality or character
voice.e: His low voice allowed him to become a bass in the choir.

wander.d: The act or instance of wandering.
wander.e: to go for a wander in the park

wave.d: To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.
wave.e: The flag waved in the gentle breeze.

weak.d: Lacking in force (usually strength) or ability.
weak.e: The child was too weak to move the boulder.

wedding.d: To perform the marriage ceremony for; to join in matrimony.
wedding.e: The wedding of our three companies took place last week.

well-known.d: Familiar, famous, renowned, noted or widely known.

while.d: An uncertain duration of time, a period of time.
while.e: He lectured for quite a long while.

whole.d: Something complete, without any parts missing.
whole.e: This variety of fascinating details didn't fall together into an enjoyable, coherent whole.

wild.d: The undomesticated state of a wild animal
wild.e: After mending the lion's leg, we returned him to the wild.

windy.e: It was a long and windy night.

wisdom.d: An element of personal character that enables one to distinguish the wise from the unwise.

wonder.d: Something that causes amazement or awe; a marvel.
wonder.e: The idea was so crazy that it is a wonder that anyone went along with it.

wood.d: The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel.
wood.e: There was lots of wood on the beach.

wooden.e: On a recent windy day, hundreds of visitors climbed wooden stairs to take pictures in front of the glacier.

wool.d: The hair of the sheep, llama and some other ruminants.

worse.e: Do not think the worse of him for his enterprise.

worst.e: My sore leg hurts worst when it's cold and rainy.

youth.d: The quality or state of being young.
youth.e: Her youth and beauty attracted him to her.
